summary.title: Police and Citizens
summary.description:
ASSUMPTIONS
1. A reverse proxy (D3) terminating TLS with the D2 certificate, and a firewall (D4), sit in front of the application and are managed by an external party. They are deliberately NOT drawn as elements in these diagrams. The controls they provide are referenced in the countermeasures of the data flows that cross the internet boundary: HTTPS-only with HSTS, certificate renewal and monitoring, request body size limits, volumetric and per-IP rate limiting, no-store cache directives on authenticated responses, and default-deny inbound rules that expose only the public HTTPS port (E15) while keeping the database listener (E19) and administrative host access (E18) off the public internet.
2. The database (D6) is reachable only from the application host (T7 -> T8). The report image store sits outside the web root and is never served directly by the web server.
3. Police officers (A3, T6) cannot create or edit reports; they may search, view, request more information and close.
4. Trust boundaries drawn as 'internet boundary' are crossed by traffic that has already passed the assumed firewall and reverse proxy.

threats.title: Weak password
threats.description: Passwords can be guessed if they are too weak
threats.mitigation:
- Enforce strong password rules such as 10 characters and at least one of capital letter, number, special character, or pass-phrases
- Limit the number of times a user can attempt to login (so that bad actors have less chances at guessing correctly)

threats.title: Citizen doesn't own email address
threats.description: The user registers with an email they don't own.
threats.mitigation: - Use email verification code after registration.

threats.title: Bad actor logs in using stolen credentials
threats.description: Bad actors finds a user's email and password (through measures like phishing emails etc) and attempts to use it to log in.
threats.mitigation:
- Implement 2 factor authentication 
- Forcing password rotation every 60 days

threats.title: Flooding the register process with get requests
threats.description: A bad actor could send many requests to the server because it is a process that does not require authentication.
threats.mitigation: - Rate limiting for requests from the same IP.

threats.title: Registration process replaced by scammer
threats.description: The official registration page has been replaced by another malicious page users are redirected to from scam emails, or text messages, or links posted online.
threats.mitigation: - Buy similar domain names with typos.

threats.title: Process leaks data via unsafe memory
threats.description: Process logs sensitive data, or stores data in unsafe (e.g., shared) memory
threats.mitigation:
- Use type-safe and memory-safe programming language e.g. Java, Rust
- Ensure log entries don't contain sensitive data.
- Monitor process usages and in/out for suspicious activity.

threats.title: Process has been tampered with - COME BACK
threats.description: The process has been altered by an external malicious actor.
threats.mitigation:
- Monitor and keep a record of process ID to identify process restart.
- Add fingerprinting to process, e.g., change time, binary / script hash.
- Monitor process in/out for suspicious activities.

threats.title: Process gets access to restricted resources
threats.description: Process runs at a higher priority level (e.g., permissions, resources), or accesses to assets outside its permission level.
threats.mitigation:
- Apply principle of least privilege for process and used resources.
- Run process on the OS with as few permissions as required, using a dedicated technical account rather than a normal user account with interactive and logon permissions.

threats.title: Injection attack - tampering
threats.description: Malicious data is passed to the process to cause harm to the underlying data, e.g., override data or inject malicious data.
threats.mitigation:
- Decode, normalise, and canonicalise email and password before validation and storage
- Sanitise input for script-like requests, e.g., javascript, SQL, etc.
- Enforce strict Content Security Policy to prevent harmful scripts to be transmitted (e.g., js, py, sh files).

threats.title: Injection attack - disclosure
threats.description: Malicious data is passed to the process to gain access to or exfiltrate data stored in database.
threats.mitigation:
- Decode, normalise, and canonicalise email and password before validation and storage
- Sanitise input from script-like statements, e.g., javascript, SQL, etc.
- Enforce strict CSP policy to prevent harmful scripts to be transmitted (e.g., js, py, sh files).

threats.title: Expose sensitive data in logs
threats.description: Logs may leak sensitive data such as email, password, IP, and session IDs, when tracing user actions.
threats.mitigation:
- Ensure that all sensitive PII data other than user ID are not logged.
- Conduct regular log audits.

threats.title: Flooding the network with traffic
threats.description: A Bad Actor floods the request channel with high-volume traffic, exhausting network/connection capacity and blocking legitimate requests from reaching the server.
threats.mitigation: - Rate limiting for requests from the same IP.

threats.title: Error messages reveal information about system state
threats.description:
An error message could contain information such as 
- server software and version
- file system paths
- stack traces
- sensitive information such as email and password
threats.mitigation:
- Don't have revealing error messages
- Use HTTPS (or another encrypted protocol) to send data over the network.

threats.title: Register process response is
threats.description: See #16

threats.title: Citizen personal data is tampered with in transit
threats.description: Bad actor changes the citizen's email and/or password so they either do not receive the verification email, or can't successfully log in.
threats.mitigation: - Use HTTPS (or another encrypted protocol) to send data over the network

threats.title: Citizen information exposed to a bad actor
threats.description: Email address and password is accessed by a bad actor on the network, allowing them to steal the user's credentials.
threats.mitigation:
- Use HTTPS (or another encrypted protocol) to send data over the network
- Use verification code to ensure stolen credentials cannot be used to log in.

threats.title: Flooding the network with traffic
threats.description: See #15

threats.title: Register process response is changed in transit
threats.description: Response html/javascript is tampered with by a bad actor e.g., injecting a malicious script, altering the form's action URL to point to an attacker-controlled endpoint, or adding a hidden field.
threats.mitigation: - Use HTTPS (or another encrypted protocol) so data is encrypted in transit

diagrams.title: Reports - Owner Access (E5-E7)
diagrams.placeholder: Owner-only report access: list (E5), create (E6) and view/edit (E7) reports. Assets: report content, report images, session identifiers. Exit point X1. | Reverse proxy (D3) and firewall (D4) are not modelled as elements: see model assumptions.

data.name: Internet boundary (T0/T3 -> T7 web application process; firewall D4 and reverse proxy D3 assumed on this line)

labels: Internet boundary (T0/T3 -> T7 web application process; firewall D4 and reverse proxy D3 assumed on this line)

data.name: Data boundary (T7 web application process -> T8 database / storage)

labels: Data boundary (T7 web application process -> T8 database / storage)

data.name:
Citizen / Report Owner
(A1, T4/T5)
data.description: A1 Citizen. T4 logged-in citizen, T5 owner of the reports they created. Registers, submits reports with images, views and edits their own open reports and generates share links.

threats.title: Session cookie theft
threats.description: A stolen session identifier lets an attacker act as the report owner (T5) without the password.
threats.mitigation: Rotate the session ID on login, apply an idle timeout and offer logout (E4).

threats.title: Citizen denies submitting a report
threats.description: The owner of a report later denies having created or edited it.
threats.mitigation: Record owner ID and timestamp on every create and edit, and retain application logs (X9) with restricted access.

data.name:
List Own Reports
(E5)
data.description: E5 Report list page. Lists reports owned by the citizen and their status. Returns exit point X1.

threats.title: Report list not scoped to owner
threats.description: A citizen could receive other reports if the query is not constrained to the authenticated owner.
threats.mitigation: Derive ownership from the session and enforce in the database query.

data.name:
Create Report
(E6)
data.description: E6 Create report page. Citizen enters the date, time, location, description and images of a new report.

threats.title: Malicious image upload
threats.description: Anything the citizen uploads is handed to the image handling library, meaning a malicious file can exploit the decoder before any content check.
threats.mitigation: Verify the bytes against permitted formats before decoding, reject on mismatch, and process images in a low-privilege sandbox.

threats.title: Image metadata disclosure
threats.description: If stripping fails or is skipped for a format, the image written to the store still carry EXIF metadata such as GPS coordinates.
threats.mitigation: Strip metadata by re-encoding rather than copying, and assert on the artefact that no EXIF or GPS block remains.

threats.title: Oversized image denial of service
threats.description: Large or resource-intensive images can consume storage and processing resources.
threats.mitigation: Enforce upload size, dimension and processing limits.

threats.title: Owner field taken from the request
threats.description: If created_by is accepted from the payload, a citizen can file a report attributed to someone else.
threats.mitigation: Set the owner from the authenticated session only and reject the field if it appears in the request.

data.name:
View / Edit Report
(E7)
data.description: E7 View and edit report page. The report owner (T5) views and edits their own report. Returns exit point X1.

threats.title: Insecure direct object reference
threats.description: A user could change the report ID to access or edit another citizen's report if the system does not check who owns it.
threats.mitigation: Derive the owner from the authenticated session and perform a server-side ownership check on the identifier for every report request.

threats.title: Editing closed reports
threats.description: A crafted request could bypass a hidden edit button if the server does not enforce report state, so a closed report can still be modified.
threats.mitigation: Always read the closed status with the record and reject updates server-side when the report is closed.

threats.title: Mass assignment of closed status
threats.description: A citizen may attempt to manipulate protected fields such as closed status.
threats.mitigation: Allow-list editable fields and never accept closed status from the citizen.

threats.title: Stored cross-site scripting in report description
threats.description: A user could enter malicious script in a report description that runs when the report is viewed.
threats.mitigation: Safely encode the report description when displaying it so it is treated as text rather than code.

data.name:
Image Handling Library
(D9)
data.description: D9 Image handling library. Processes uploaded report images and writes them to storage.

threats.title: Vulnerable image parser
threats.description: A crafted image exploits a decoder flaw in D9 and executes code as the T7 application identity.
threats.mitigation: Restrict decoding to an allow-list of formats, and process images in a low-privilege sandboxed worker.

threats.title: Decompression bomb exhausts memory
threats.description: A small file that expands to an enormous bitmap consumes all memory and CPU during processing.
threats.mitigation: Enforce maximum pixel dimensions and total pixel count before decoding, plus per-image processing timeouts and memory caps.

threats.title: Image path derived from client input
threats.description: A user could manipulate the image filename to access or store files outside the intended image storage location.
threats.mitigation: Generate image filenames on the server and only allow files to be stored and retrieved from the designated image directory.

data.name:
Report Store
(D6)
data.description: D6 Database. Asset: report content - date, time, location, description, created time, closed status and owner / created_by. Reachable only from the application (T7 -> T8).

threats.title: Unauthorised report disclosure
threats.description: Direct database access could expose sensitive report information.
threats.mitigation: Restrict database access, use least privilege and protect data at rest.

threats.title: Direct report tampering
threats.description: Database access could bypass application authorisation and modify reports.
threats.mitigation: Restrict direct database access and audit administrative changes.

data.name: Report Image Store
data.description: Asset: report images. Uploaded photographs related to an incident, written by D9 and read back by E10. Held outside the web root.

threats.title: Unauthorised image retrieval
threats.description: Image files can be read straight from storage, bypassing the report-level authorisation performed by E10.
threats.mitigation: Keep the image store outside the web root so files are never served directly; only E10 may read it, using the T7 application identity.

data.name: Query report store for citizen's own reports

threats.title: Owner predicate omitted or injected
threats.description: If the owner constraint is built by string concatenation it can be removed or subverted, returning every citizen's reports.
threats.mitigation: Parameterised queries with the owner value bound from the session, and never accept the owner from the request.

labels: Query report store for citizen's own reports

threats.title: Over-broad result set returned to the application
threats.description: Selecting whole rows pulls back columns the list page never renders, widening what a later flaw could leak.
threats.mitigation: Select only the columns the listing needs.

threats.title: Malicious image upload
threats.description: This flow is the unvalidated file as it reaches D9. See the identically titled threat on Create Report (E6) for the full description.
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Create Report (E6).

threats.title: Image metadata disclosure
threats.description: The image on this flow is only sanitised if stripping actually succeeded for its format. See the identically titled threat on Create Report (E6) for the full description.
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Create Report (E6).

threats.title: Image path derived from client input
threats.description: The filename carried on this flow is used to build the write path. See the identically titled threat on Image Handling Library (D9) for the full description.
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Image Handling Library (D9).

threats.title: SQL injection on the report write path
threats.description: Unparameterised report fields on insert (E6) or update (E7) let an attacker alter or destroy data in D6, including rows beyond their own report.
threats.mitigation: Use parameterised queries or ORM binding for every insert and update, and give the T7 account only the privileges it needs on D6.

threats.title: Confirmation discloses internal identifiers
threats.description: Returning database keys or storage paths in the report creation response tells an attacker how to address other records.
threats.mitigation: Return only the fields the citizen needs with no internal identifiers and no stack traces, use generic error messages.

threats.title: Editing closed reports
threats.description: This flow is where the closed status must be carried into the edit decision. See the identically titled threat on View / Edit Report (E7) for the full description.
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on View / Edit Report (E7).

threats.title: SQL injection on the report write path
threats.description: This flow carries the update values. See the identically titled threat on new report record + owner for the full description.
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on new report record + owner.

threats.title: Report data cached by the browser or an intermediary
threats.description: The report detail response is authenticated content crossing the internet boundary. See the identically titled threat on owned report list (X1) for the full description.
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on owned report list (X1).

threats.title: Session cookie intercepted in transit
threats.description: The session identifier authenticates every subsequent request, observed on the network it allows full impersonation of the report owner (T5).
threats.mitigation: HTTPS only and a short idle timeout.

threats.title: Request flooding on the report list
threats.description: Repeated list requests force repeated database queries and deny the service to other citizens.
threats.mitigation: Per-session and per-IP rate limiting in the application.

data.name: new report submission (date, time, location, description, images)

threats.title: Report content and incident location observed in transit
threats.description: The submission carries the incident location and description, which are sensitive to the reporting citizen.
threats.mitigation: HTTPS only with HSTS (D2/D3, see model assumptions).

threats.title: Report altered in transit
threats.description: An attacker on the path modifies the incident detail or substitutes the uploaded images before they reach E6.
threats.mitigation: Use HTTPS/TLS to protect the data while it is being transmitted.

threats.title: Oversized multipart upload exhausts capacity
threats.description: A very large upload ties up connections and disk before E6 can reject it.
threats.mitigation: Enforce a request body size limit and an upload timeout.

labels: new report submission (date, time, location, description, images)

threats.title: Insecure direct object reference
threats.description: This flow carries the client-supplied report ID that can be altered. See the identically titled threat on View / Edit Report (E7) for the full description.
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on View / Edit Report (E7).

threats.title: Edited report content observed in transit
threats.description: Both the retrieved report and the edited version cross the internet boundary in this exchange.
threats.mitigation: HTTPS only with HSTS (see model assumptions).

threats.title: Report data cached by the browser or an intermediary
threats.description: A cached listing or report page can be recovered from a shared machine after logout, or served to another user by a shared cache.
threats.mitigation: Disable caching for report routes at the assumed reverse proxy (D3).

threats.title: Error responses reveal application state
threats.description: Stack traces or framework error pages disclose D5 versions and file system paths.
threats.mitigation: Return generic error pages and log the detail server-side only (X9).

diagrams.title: Reports - Share Links (E8-E9)
diagrams.placeholder: Share-link lifecycle: creating a link (E8) and validating a token to show a report (E9). Assets: share tokens, report content. Exit point X2. | Reverse proxy (D3) and firewall (D4) are not modelled as elements: see model assumptions.

data.name:
Citizen / Report Owner
(A1, T4/T5)
data.description: A1 Citizen. T4 logged-in citizen, T5 owner of the reports they created. Registers, submits reports with images, views and edits their own open reports and generates share links.

threats.title: Session cookie theft
threats.description: A stolen session lets an attacker create share links for the victim's reports.
threats.mitigation: HTTPS only, session rotation on login and an idle timeout.

data.name:
Share-link Recipient
(A2, T3)
data.description: A2 Share-link recipient. T3 unauthenticated user holding a valid share token received outside the system. Never authenticates and is unknown to the system.

threats.title: Share-link recipient is not authenticated
threats.description: T3 has no identity in the system an attacker holding the URL is indistinguishable from the person the owner meant to share the report with.
threats.mitigation: Expose nothing through the share view that assumes the viewer is the intended recipient.

data.name:
Random Number Generator
(D8)
data.description: D8 Random number generator. Produces the share tokens (and the E2 verification codes).

threats.title: Predictable token
threats.description: A seeded or non-cryptographic generator produces guessable tokens, letting an attacker forge a working share link and read a report without ever being given the link.
threats.mitigation: Generate share tokens using a cryptographically secure random source, don't use a seeded random number generator

data.name:
Create Share Link
(E8)
data.description: E8 Share link creation. The action which creates the secret link for a report owned by the citizen.

threats.title: Predictable token
threats.description: E8 gets the token from D8, so it inherits whatever entropy D8 provides. See the identically titled threat on Random Number Generator (D8).
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Random Number Generator (D8).

threats.title: Creating a link for someone else's report
threats.description: A citizen submits another citizen's report ID to E8 and obtains a working share link for a report they do not own.
threats.mitigation: Server side ownership check before creating the token.

threats.title: Share tokens stored in usable form
threats.description: See the identically titled threat on Share Token Store (D6).
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Share Token Store (D6).

threats.title: Cross-site request forgery creates a share link
threats.description: A third party page causes a logged in owner's browser to create a share link, which the attacker then reads from a page or email.
threats.mitigation: Require an CSRF token on the share link action.

data.name:
Validate Token and Show Report
(E9)
data.description: E9 Share link page. The public address that receives a secret token and, if the token is valid, shows the matching report. Returns exit point X2.

threats.title: Token enumeration
threats.description: An attacker submits large numbers of candidate tokens hoping to hit a valid one.
threats.mitigation: Use generic responses for invalid tokens, rate limiting and alerting on sustained invalid token rates.

threats.title: Closed report remains accessible
threats.description: A share link created while the report was open keeps returning content after closure if report state is not re-checked during share-link authorisation.
threats.mitigation: Re-check the report state at read time and refuse the share view for closed reports.

threats.title: Share token reains valid indefinitely once leaked
threats.description: The specified system provides no expiry or revocation for share tokens, so a token that leaks grants access to the report permanently.
threats.mitigation: Keep the token out of search indexes, caches and access logs, and rate-limit validation

data.name:
Report Store
(D6)
data.description: D6 Database. Asset: report content - date, time, location, description, created time, closed status and owner / created_by. Reachable only from the application (T7 -> T8).

threats.title: Unauthorised report disclosure
threats.description: Direct database access could expose sensitive report information.
threats.mitigation: Restrict database access, use least privilege and protect data at rest.

threats.title: Direct report tampering
threats.description: Database access could bypass application authorisation and modify reports.
threats.mitigation: Restrict direct database access and audit administrative changes.

data.name:
Share Token Store
(D6)
data.description: D6 Database. Asset: share tokens - secret values granting read access to one report without logging in, with their report association, expiry and revocation state.

threats.title: Share tokens stored in usable form
threats.description: Anyone who reads the share token store obtains all working share links.
threats.mitigation: Write only a cryptographic hash of the token, plaintext should exist solely in the URL returned to the owner.

threats.title: Share token reains valid indefinitely once leaked
threats.description: See the identically titled threat on Validate Token and Show Report (E9) for the full description.
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Validate Token and Show Report (E9).

threats.title: Predictable token
threats.description: This flow carries the generated token, so its value is only as unguessable as the source that produced it. See the threat on Random Number Generator (D8) for the full description.
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Random Number Generator (D8).

threats.title: Share tokens stored in usable form
threats.description: This flow is what reaches the store, so is carrying the plaintext token. See the identically titled threat on Share Token Store (D6) for the full description.
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Share Token Store (D6).

threats.title: Token leaks through header, browser history or logs
threats.description: The secret token sits in the URL, therefore anyone with log access thereby gains report access.
threats.mitigation: Never log the token or full query strings, don't include share token in proxy logs, and keep the token lifetime short.

threats.title: Recipient forwards the share link
threats.description: A share token is a bearer credential, so anyone the recipient passes it to gains the same read access.
threats.mitigation: Treat any token holder as anonymous and untrusted: the share view returns report content only.

threats.title: Token enumeration
threats.description: This flow is the endpoint the candidate tokens are submitted against where attackers are guessing. See the identically titled threat on Validate Token and Show Report (E9).
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Validate Token and Show Report (E9).

threats.title: Candidate token injected into the lookup query
threats.description: The candidate token is supplied by an unauthenticated caller and may contain SQL injection code.
threats.mitigation: Use paramaterisation to prevent SQL injection.

threats.title: Closed report remains accessible
threats.description: This flow must carry the report's current closed state so E9 can check it at read time. See the identically titled threat on Validate Token and Show Report (E9).
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Validate Token and Show Report (E9).

threats.title: Report identifier substituted after token validation
threats.description: If the report ID comes from the request rather than the token record, a valid token can be pointed at any report.
threats.mitigation: Resolve the report identifier exclusively from the stored token association, ignore any report ID in the request.

threats.title: Closed report remains accessible
threats.description: This flow is the report content returned after that check should have run. See the identically titled threat on Validate Token and Show Report (E9) for the full description.
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Validate Token and Show Report (E9).

threats.title: Shared report cached by an intermediary
threats.description: The share page is unauthenticated, so a shared cache is more likely to store and re-serve it.
threats.mitigation: Don't cache on the share response, reinforced at the assumed reverse proxy (D3).

threats.title: Share-link request observed in transit
threats.description: The request reveals which report is about to be shared, and the response carries the resulting secret URL.
threats.mitigation: HTTPS only with HSTS.

threats.title: Unbounded token generation for a single report
threats.description: Repeatedly requesting share links for the same report creates an unbounded set of simultaneously valid tokens and consumes storage in the token store.
threats.mitigation: Cap the number of active share links per report and per citizen, and expire or revoke a superseded token when a new one is issued for the same report.

threats.title: Share token observed in transit
threats.description: The token is a bearer credential carried in the URL, so anyone who observes the request gains the same read access as the recipient.
threats.mitigation: HTTPS only with HSTS

threats.title: Token leaks through Referer header, browser history or logs
threats.description: The token travels in the URL on this request as well. See the identically titled threat on share URL for the full description.
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on share URL.

diagrams.title: Reports - Officer Access (E11-E14)
diagrams.placeholder: Officer handling of reports: search (E11), view details (E12), request more information (E13) and close (E14). Exit points X3, X6, X7. | Reverse proxy (D3) and firewall (D4) are not modelled as elements: see model assumptions.

data.name:
Police Officer
(A3, T6)
data.description: A3 Police officer. T6 logged-in police officer: searches and views all reports, emails owners requesting more information and closes reports. Assumed unable to create or edit reports.

threats.title: Officer account compromised
threats.description: An attacker holding officer credentials, or an intercepted officer session, reads every report in the system and can close any of them.
threats.mitigation: Serve officer routes over HTTPS with HSTS, apply a short idle timeout and alert on unusual sign in locations.

threats.title: Privileged officer action not recorded
threats.description: There is no record of which officer performed a privileged action like closures or requesting further information
threats.mitigation: Write an audit record of officer ID, action, related text, timestamp, and protect the logs (X9) from the T6 role.

data.name:
Citizen / Report Owner
(A1, T4/T5)
data.description: A1 Citizen. T4 logged-in citizen, T5 owner of the reports they created. Registers, submits reports with images, views and edits their own open reports and generates share links.

threats.title: Report owner's mailbox controlled by an attacker
threats.description: An attacker who controls the report owner's mailbox receives the information request (X6) and the closure notification (X7)
threats.mitigation: Re-verify the address whenever it is changed, and keep incident detail out of  email by linking back to the authenticated page.

data.name:
Report Search
(E11)
data.description: E11 Report search page. The form where an officer searches reports by date, location, status or keyword. Returns exit point X3.

threats.title: Search injection
threats.description: Keyword and filter values are attacker influenced input. If they are concatenated into the query rather than bound, an attacker can read or alter data in D6.
threats.mitigation: Parameterised queries and treat every search term as data, never as query syntax.

threats.title: Search accessible without the officer role
threats.description: A logged-in citizen (T4) reaching the search route would obtain reports belonging to everyone.
threats.mitigation: Enforce the T6 role server-side on the route itself, not only by hiding the navigation link.

threats.title: Unbounded search scans the whole store
threats.description: Leading wildcard or empty-criteria searches force a full scan of every report in D6, denying the service to other users.
threats.mitigation: Paginate results, apply query timeouts and index the searchable columns.

data.name:
Full Report Details
(E12)
data.description: E12 Officer report details page. The page where an officer views the full details of any report. Returns exit point X3.

threats.title: Bulk harvesting of reports
threats.description: An officer account enumerates and exports every report, including incident locations and images
threats.mitigation: rate limit searches, log every access with officer ID, and alert on abnormal viewing volume.

threats.title: Role check missing on the detail page
threats.description: The detail route is reachable by a non-officer session if authorisation is only applied at menu rendering.
threats.mitigation: Verify the T6 role server-side on every request to the officer detail route.

data.name:
Request More Info
(E13)
data.description: E13 Request more info form. The form where an officer provides the extra details required, which the system emails to the report owner. Produces exit point X6.

threats.title: Email header injection
threats.description: Injecting extra headers, letting the message be redirected or additional recipients added.
threats.mitigation: Include input validataion and construct headers through the mail library rather than by string building.

threats.title: Information request sent to the wrong owner
threats.description: The recipient address is taken from the request instead of the stored report, so report detail reaches an attacker chosen mailbox.
threats.mitigation: Resolve the recipient from the report's stored owner in D6, never from client supplied input.

threats.title: Report content disclosed in cleartext email
threats.description: Mail delivery to the citizen's external provider is outside the system's control so any incident detail ends up in an external mailbox in cleartext.
threats.mitigation: Keep incident detail out of the message body, send a short notice identifying the report by reference with a link back to the authenticated page

data.name:
Close Report
(E14)
data.description: E14 Close report action. The action which closes a report and notifies its owner. Produces exit point X7.

threats.title: Unauthorised closure of a report
threats.description: A crafted request from a citizen session closes a report, which would also stop the owner editing it (see E7).
threats.mitigation: Enforce the T6 role server-side on the close action and reject the closed field on any citizen facing endpoint.

threats.title: Privileged officer action not recorded
threats.description: E14 is where the closure is written and must record who set it. See the identically titled threat on Police Officer (A3, T6)
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Police Officer (A3, T6).

threats.title: Cross site request forgery closes a report
threats.description: A closure is irreversible for the owner, who can no longer edit the report afterwards.
threats.mitigation: Require a CSRF token on the close action.

data.name:
Email Dispatcher
(D10)
data.description: D10 Email dispatcher. Sends the verification, information request and closure emails to the citizen's external email provider.

threats.title: Mail credentials disclosed
threats.description: Mail service credentials stored in the application configuration are read by an attacker, who can then send mail as the service.
threats.mitigation: Keep configuration outside the web root, readable only by the T7 account, and rotate credentials.

threats.title: Dispatcher abused to send arbitrary mail
threats.description: An attacker who can reach the dispatcher sends convincing mail that appears to come from the service, enabling phishing against citizens.
threats.mitigation: Authenticate which accounts have access to the mail service,

threats.title: Email queue flooded
threats.description: Repeated information requests or closures generate enough mail to exhaust the sending quota, delaying verification email (X5) and blocking registration.
threats.mitigation: Rate limit outbound mail per officer and per report.

data.name:
Report Store
(D6)
data.description: D6 Database. Asset: report content - date, time, location, description, created time, closed status and owner / created_by. Reachable only from the application (T7 -> T8).

threats.title: Unauthorised report disclosure
threats.description: Direct database access could expose sensitive report information.
threats.mitigation: Restrict database access, use least privilege and protect data at rest.

threats.title: Direct report tampering
threats.description: Database access could bypass application authorisation and modify reports.
threats.mitigation: Restrict direct database access and audit administrative changes.

threats.title: Unbounded search scans the whole store
threats.description: This flow is the query that reaches D6. See the identically titled threat on Report Search (E11) for the full description.
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Report Search (E11).

threats.title: More columns returned than the page renders
threats.description: Returning every column of every match exposes citizen account identifiers alongside the incident record.
threats.mitigation: Return only the columns the page renders, no citizen personal data.

threats.title: Bulk harvesting of citizen reports
threats.description: Repeated wide searches harvest the database through this flow. See the identically titled threat on Full Report Details (E12).
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Full Report Details (E12).

threats.title: More columns returned than the page renders
threats.description: The detail read pulls the owner's account identifiers alongside the incident record. See the identically titled threat on matching reports.
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on matching reports.

threats.title: Bulk harvesting of citizen reports
threats.description: Every detail view leaves the system on this flow, so repeated views are how the harvesting actually happens. See the identically titled threat on Full Report Details (E12).
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Full Report Details (E12).

threats.title: Privileged officer action not recorded
threats.description: This flow is the audit write for an information request by a Police offer. See the identically titled threat on Police Officer (A3, T6).
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Police Officer (A3, T6).

threats.title: Email header injection
threats.description: This flow hands the officer supplied text and recipient address to D10 where injected header lines would take effect. See the identically titled threat on Request More Info (E13).
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Request More Info (E13).

threats.title: Report content disclosed in cleartext email
threats.description: The information request email leaves the system on this flow. See the identically titled threat on Request More Info (E13).
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Request More Info (E13).

data.name: set closed status + closing officer + timestamp

threats.title: Privileged officer action not recorded
threats.description: This flow is the closure write that must carry the closing officer and timestamp in the same statement. See the identically titled threat on Police Officer (A3, T6).
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Police Officer (A3, T6).

labels: set closed status + closing officer + timestamp

threats.title: Report content disclosed in cleartext email
threats.description: This flow hands the closure notification and the owner's address to D10 for delivery outside the system. See the identically titled threat on Request More Info (E13).
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Request More Info (E13).

threats.title: Report content disclosed in cleartext email
threats.description: The closure notification leaves the system on this flow and may quote the incident. See the identically titled threat on Request More Info (E13).
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Request More Info (E13).

threats.title: Search injection
threats.description: This flow carries the attacker-influenced search terms into E11. See the identically titled threat on Report Search (E11).
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Report Search (E11).

threats.title: Role check missing on the detail page
threats.description: This flow carries the session and the client supplied report ID that E12 must authorise on every request. See the identically titled threat on Full Report Details (E12).
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Full Report Details (E12).

threats.title: Report identifier substituted to close an unrelated report
threats.description: The report ID is client supplied and could be changed to close a report the officer did not intend.
threats.mitigation: Require an explicit confirmation step and record the closing officer and timestamp for audit.

data.name: officer session + report ID + information request text

threats.title: Information request text observed in transit
threats.description: The text may quote incident detail from the report.
threats.mitigation: Use HTTPS protocol only with HSTS .

data.description: Search query for full report details

threats.title: Search injection
threats.description: The identifier E12 looks up is client supplied and reaches D6 on this flow. See the identically titled threat on Report Search (E11).
threats.mitigation: See the identically titled threat on Report Search (E11).
